narration.headline: different properties: correlation -0.0172 across 25 cells; the other statistics compare different quantities
narration.framing: model-vs-model agreement (no ground truth), not accuracy

result.method: pointwise pixel-value sampled on a grid over the shared extent (an estimate, not every pixel); windows where either map is no-data are dropped before any statistic; no ground truth, so this is model-vs-model agreement (no ground truth), not accuracy.
result.warning: the results measure different properties (['sample_karst_score', 'sample_number']), so their values are different quantities: only the correlation (whether they rise and fall together) is meaningful. Do not read the mean difference, RMSE or agreement fraction as a gap between them, and do not say one reads higher than the other.
result.nodata_rule: a sample is no-data, and never enters a statistic, when its band is missing or NaN, equals the model's nodata_value, lies outside the band's declared regression range, or carries no class on a classification band

content:
Compared both 2025 PA Karst predictions on their shared extent. Key point first: **I can't tell you which is right** — neither has ground-truth labels, so this is model-vs-model comparison only, and the two maps output different quantities (`sample_karst_score` [0–1] vs `sample_number` [0.2–1.2]).

| Metric | Value | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Correlation | -0.017 (≈0) | They do not rise/fall together at all |
| Samples | 25 of 72 grid cells | 47 dropped as no-data/off-raster |
| Agreement (±0.1) | 0% | Not meaningful — different units, ignore |

**Where they differ:** effectively everywhere sampleable — the near-zero correlation means the two layers describe spatially unrelated patterns over the ~10,091 km² shared area. Do not read the mean gap or RMSE as a real difference, since the properties aren't the same quantity.

To find out which is *right* you'd need labels: I can plan a small labeling effort on one map (confidence-targeted windows from `olmoearth_plan_label_sample`) so you mark karst present/absent on a few dozen points, then compute an error rate and per-class metrics with `olmoearth_classification_metrics`. Want me to set that up for one of the two?
